newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says considering 30-year dollar bond.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says considering 30-year dollar bond.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Thursday he is considering a proposal to issue a 30-year dollar bond in the international market.
"The Central Bank is being offered 30-year money. We are still studying it," Singson told Reuters.
He said the proposal came from Morgan Stanley about two weeks ago, which offered to raise funds for the country at the cost of about 250 basis points above the comparable U.S. Treasury.
"Before that they were saying 20 years, and then I said 'if it's 30 years, I might consider it'," Singson added. He declined to say how much money would be raised in the offer.
Last September the Philippines issued 20-year uncollateralised Brady bonds at 225 basis points over the comparable U.S. Treasury.
